{
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "asset_category", "analytical_usefulness": 0.9, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Categorizing spend into asset types (laptop, cloud_service, etc.) gives a strong new grouping axis for expense analysis. Values are well-grounded in short_description/ci text; minor concern is 'cloud_service' inferred for 'iPod touch/ISP Services' which is a defensible reading.", "hallucination_observed": false},
    {"name": "asset_brand", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.8, "rationale": "Brand extraction (Dell, HP, Lenovo) is genuinely useful for vendor/spend concentration analysis. Extractions like Dell XPS 13 -> Dell are sound. Weakness: 'other_hardware' is used as a brand fallback (category leakage), which is a slightly muddled but not fabricated value.", "hallucination_observed": false},
    {"name": "spend_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.6, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "A coarser spend classification (physical_hardware, travel, cloud) is useful but largely redundant with asset_category, offering limited additional leverage. Values are well-grounded in source text.", "hallucination_observed": false},
    {"name": "travel_flag", "analytical_usefulness": 0.45, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "A bare travel boolean is derivable and mildly useful for segmenting, but it is largely a restatement of spend_type/asset_category (travel_expense/travel_equipment) and is a generic binary flag with limited new leverage.", "hallucination_observed": false},
    {"name": "asset_lifecycle_action", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "rationale": "Lifecycle action (registration, allocation, provisioning) adds a process/operational axis useful for actionability. Reasonably grounded in verbs of short_description, though 'registration' dominating heavily and specifics like 'allocation' for 'Asset assignment' are somewhat inferred.", "hallucination_observed": false},
    {"name": "record_origin", "analytical_usefulness": 0.4, "source_groundedness": 0.5, "rationale": "manual_entry vs auto_generated could be actionable, but the source basis is unclear; the table has no explicit origin field, so the true/false split appears heuristic and weakly grounded, and the flag itself is generic.", "hallucination_observed": true},
    {"name": "processing_lag_band", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Binning the gap between opened_at and processed_date is a strong actionable axis (backlog, unprocessed records). Well-grounded: 'nan' processed_date maps to 'not_processed' correctly and dated rows get plausible bands.", "hallucination_observed": false},
    {"name": "has_source_id", "analytical_usefulness": 0.35, "source_groundedness": 0.95, "rationale": "A presence/absence flag on an existing column (source_id) is trivially redundant with an original column and adds little analytical leverage, though it is perfectly grounded.", "hallucination_observed": false},
    {"name": "high_volume_user_flag", "analytical_usefulness": 0.55, "source_groundedness": 0.55, "rationale": "A high-volume user flag could help identify heavy spenders, but it is a coarse derived binary; its threshold and basis are opaque and the near-even split raises questions about how faithfully it reflects the underlying user frequency.", "hallucination_observed": false}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.62,
  "source_groundedness": 0.77,
  "rationale": "The strongest columns (asset_category, asset_brand, processing_lag_band, asset_lifecycle_action) give genuine new axes for grouping expense records by asset type, vendor, backlog, and process state, and are mostly sound readings of short_description/ci/date fields. Several columns are weaker: spend_type and travel_flag largely restate asset_category; has_source_id is trivially redundant with an existing column. record_origin and high_volume_user_flag have opaque source bases and some heuristic assertion that the text does not clearly support. Groundedness is generally good, with reasonable handling of silent/nan rows, but 'other_hardware' leaking into asset_brand and the origin heuristic are the main concerns."
}
